feedback.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z={x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}$ at the point $(1,2,-1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2xy \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}y-{y}^{3}) \\  & =2xy+{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2) & =3(1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+2(1)(2)=11 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) & =2(1)(2)+{1}^{2}-3(2)^{2}=-7\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-(-1) & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,2)+(y-2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,2) \\ z+1 & =11(x-1)-7(y-2) \\ z+1 & =11x-7y+3 \\ -11x+7y+z-2 & =0 \\ 11x-7y-z+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
